auto_merge.commit_message:
It's a special case that is not special enough to break the rules. `special_bool_compare_function` came later and is now capable of covering the same.

Along the way, optimises `'c' in str`, `b'c' in bytes`, `char in bytearray`.

Closes https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/3888

comment_data.body:
It is a bit clumsy to return a flag and a node. But what I really like about this is that it moves all decisions into `find_special_bool_compare_function()` and coerces both operands as needed, in one place.

I considered returning only the coerced operand node or None (to say that no special case matched), but I failed to find a good name for such a function. It seems more explicit to return both.

comment_data.body: This limitation is gone. I found it difficult to distribute the implementation over `CmpNode` and `PrimaryCmpNode` and ran into issues with `CascadedCmpNode`, so I fixed up the implementation until it no longer complained. But this is a new feature as well that is not thoroughly tested. Good thing is that it was previously forbidden, so existing code cannot use it. And code with cascaded comparisons is probably rare outside of numeric ranges, so not very likely to appear for strings in combination with `in` tests.

comment_data.body:
One variantion that I don't think you've tested is a single character literal as the middle argument, e.g.

```
c in "f" in some_str
```

Just because the single character literal is special-cased when on the left-hand side but not when on the right-hand side so I can see there's potential to go wrong there.

(I haven't tested this myself either so it's a suggestion of what could go wrong rather than something I believe does go wrong)

commit.message: Optimise "'c' in str" and "b'c' in bytes" and also "char in bytearray".
Add tests for single character in cascade.
Call "PyUnicode_READY()" in Py<3.12 before making use of Unicode internals.

commit.message: Remove special cases from "__Pyx_PyUnicode_ContainsTF()" since none of them proved worth it.
Improve special cases in "__Pyx_UnicodeContainsUCS4()", giving -30 to -50% in suitable cases.
Change C guard: we are not using PyUnicode internals but just the C-API for it, but that is unlikely to be fast in anything but CPython.
